checks.label: Completing the square is a technique for manipulating a quadratic into a perfect square plus a constant: on every screen, at every setting of b, the finished form drawn agrees with the screen's quadratic at every x tried
In modern notation ax^2 + bx + c converts to a(x + b/(2a))^2 + (c − b^2/(4a)): every screen's bracket number is b ÷ 2a and its number outside is c − b² ÷ 4a, for a = 1, 2 and −1 alike

The coordinates of the turning point and the equation of the line of symmetry can be found by writing the quadratic expression in completed square form: every marked turning point sits at (−h, k) of that form, every line of symmetry at x = −h, the slope there is zero and the curve is mirrored about it

The tiles add up: at every b from 0 to 10, the square, its two half strips and the empty corner exactly fill a square of side x + b ÷ 2 without overlapping, and the corner reads (b ÷ 2)², which is 0, 1, 4, 9, 16 and 25

Every puzzle accepts only its right answer, worked out from its rule; each wrong pick, put into the rule at its check value, gives a different number, and a point on the curve that is not the turning point sits higher than it

The worked numbers: 1 + 6 = 7 and 16 − 9 = 7 at x = 1; the wrong picks give 36, 21, 14, 10, 67, 14, 59 and 105; √7 is about 2.65, the roots are about −0.35, −5.65, −0.27 and −3.73; (−5, −23) at b = 10; and the practice form 2(x − 3)² + 7 gives 18 + 7 = 25 at x = 0

As b grows from 0 to 10 the lowest point slides left to x = −b ÷ 2 and drops below the plain number by exactly the corner, from (0, 0) to (−5, −25), and the drop on the graph is the corner under the tiles

Before Check a puzzle shows no curve and no finished form; after a right answer the curve is drawn whole with its turning point, roots or completed corner, and a wrong pick puts its own number in, in red
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s

warnings: SVG labels "x² + 6x" and "= (x + 3)² − 9" are touching on one row, so they read as one: leave at least 4 px between them, or label only what differs (at the opening state, and 22 more settings)
